This connects back to the randomness versus quality tradeoff, already covered generally in Sampling. Sampling genuinely needs a way to tune how much randomness actually goes into that tradeoff.
Temperature genuinely provides exactly that one, simple, tunable control, the exact mechanism explored throughout the rest of this topic.
4. How Temperature Rescales The Distribution
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292602-698329946.png

This connects back to the randomness versus quality tradeoff, already covered in this topic. Temperature genuinely divides each raw score before the softmax function, already covered generally in Attention Mechanism, converts them to probabilities.
This genuinely rescaling directly changes how sharp or flat the resulting probability distribution becomes, the genuinely core mechanical detail explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 5. Low Temperature Behavior
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292603-535681016.png

This connects back to how temperature rescales the distribution, already covered in this topic. A genuinely low temperature genuinely sharpens the distribution toward the single highest probability word.

This genuinely approaches greedy decoding, already covered generally in Sampling, as temperature genuinely approaches zero, a genuinely useful limiting case explored throughout the rest of this topic.
6. High Temperature Behavior
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292947-163180240.png
This connects back to low temperature behavior, already covered in this topic. A genuinely high temperature genuinely flattens the distribution, spreading probability more evenly.
This genuinely increases the chance that lower probability, more surprising words actually get picked, the genuinely opposite effect explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This flattening effect, already covered in this topic, directly explains why very high temperature settings can eventually produce genuinely incoherent output, since even very unlikely words start receiving meaningful probability.

blocks.text: 7. Temperature Equals One
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292948-856468020.png
This connects back to low and high temperature behavior, both already covered in this topic. A temperature of genuinely exactly one leaves the original distribution genuinely completely unchanged.
This genuinely serves as the natural, neutral baseline between those two extremes already covered in this topic, a genuinely useful reference point explored throughout the rest of this topic.

9. Recognizing When To Genuinely Adjust Temperature

blocks.alt: Recognizing When To Genuinely Adjust Temperature
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446292950-679470400.png

This connects back to genuinely low temperature sharpening toward the top word, already covered in this topic. Lower temperature, already covered in this topic, genuinely suits tasks needing consistent, reliable answers.

This connects back to genuinely high temperature spreading probability more evenly, already covered in this topic. Higher temperature, already covered, genuinely suits tasks wanting varied, creative output instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates rescaling a probability distribution with different temperature values, already covered in this topic.

code.content:
import math

def apply_temperature(scores, temperature):
    # already covered as how temperature rescales the distribution in this topic
    scaled = [s / temperature for s in scores]
    exp_scores = [math.exp(s) for s in scaled]
    total = sum(exp_scores)
    return [e / total for e in exp_scores]

raw_scores = {"mat": 2.0, "rug": 1.0, "floor": 0.5}  # already covered as raw scores in this topic
words = list(raw_scores.keys())
scores = list(raw_scores.values())

for temperature in [0.2, 1.0, 2.0]:
    # already covered as low, neutral, and high temperature behavior in this topic
    probs = apply_temperature(scores, temperature)
    formatted = {w: round(p, 3) for w, p in zip(words, probs)}
    print(f"Temperature={temperature}: {formatted}")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the same raw scores producing a sharply peaked distribution at low temperature and a much flatter distribution at high temperature, exactly the rescaling behavior already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Temperature is one number controlling how sharp or flat the sampling distribution becomes.
It provides a tunable control over the randomness versus quality tradeoff already covered in Sampling.
Temperature divides raw scores before the softmax function converts them into probabilities.
Low temperature sharpens the distribution, approaching greedy decoding as it approaches zero.
High temperature flattens the distribution, increasing the chance of surprising word choices.
A temperature of exactly one leaves the original distribution completely unchanged.
Factual, deterministic tasks typically prefer lower temperature; creative tasks prefer higher temperature.
Very high temperature can eventually produce incoherent output as unlikely words gain real probability.
Next up: Top-k Sampling, a technique restricting choices to only the most likely tokens.
